coats-seams.title: Coats — Seam Types (ISO 4916 seam classes / ISO 4915 stitch types)
quotes: For the seam specification to be meaningful, the designation of the stitch type has to be added after the designation of the stitched seam.
coats-seams.note: The two ISO numbers, the plain-seam pair (1.01.01 + 301), the serging code (6.01.01) and the bound class (3) are all stated verbatim in the source or in knowledge/DIKIS-SOZLUGU-ISO-2026-08-23.md §3. The 2.5 mm stitch length is the standard lockstitch setting quoted alongside; it is a SETTING, not a tolerance, and nothing in the engine reads it.

unl-knits.title: University of Nebraska–Lincoln extension, Sewing With Knits (the 4-inch stretch test)
quotes: plain straight stitch (seams pop; use narrow zigzag 1-1.5mm)
unl-knits.note: Mirrored in knowledge/stitchu.db, table `fabrics`, row 'jersey' (columns stretch / common_mistakes). ⚠ UNL's band edges are NOT the band this engine drafts on — see fabricease.hpp: the F-H card's band is implemented and UNL is recorded as the cross-reference, not averaged in.

iso-4915.title: ISO 4915:1991 — Textiles, Stitch types, classification and terminology
quotes: 6 classes: 100 chain · 200 hand-origin · 300 lockstitch · 400 multi-thread chain · 500 overedge · 600 covering
First digit = class, second and third = type within class.
iso-4915.note: Read in knowledge/DIKIS-SOZLUGU-ISO-2026-08-23.md §2. Only class numbers and 301 are quoted by the engine; a 3-digit type is never invented from the class.
